newsitem.title: USA: AmEx sues First USA over credit card trademark.
newsitem.headline: AmEx sues First USA over credit card trademark.

text.p: American Express Co. has sued First USA Bank alleging the rival credit card distributor infringed on its "Platinum Card" trademark, according to court papers.

In papers filed late Thursday in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, the New York-based travel and financial services company said it first used the "Platinum Card" mark in 1984 and registered it in 1992.
Emily Porter, a spokeswoman with American Express, said the company has not actually served the lawsuit on the Dallas-based credit card company because it hopes to resolve the dispute.
"We've sent them a letter and hope they respond to it", Porter said.
First USA spokesman David Webster said "We believe that American Express' claim to the words 'Platinum Card' as we use them is without merit."
"We believe American Express should compete with us in the marketplace and not attack us in the courthouse. They tried this same tactic in 1988 with the gold card and lost," he continued.
"Ours is a no fee card with competitive interest rates. Theirs comes with a $300 annual fee and their customers must pay their balance in full each month," he said.

When asked if American Express intended to sue Wilmington, Del.-based bank MBNA Corp., which launched a "Platinum Plus" card earlier this year, Porter said the two trademarks are not exactly the same.
"We have not sued MBNA, but we are watching them," Porter said.
The lawsuit seeks an injunction against First USA's continued alleged infringement and unspecified damages tripled for "willfulness."
